sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Dvaita Vedanta**: The philosophy of **Dualism**, asserting that God (Vishnu) and the individual soul are fundamentally different entities.
• **Tattvavada**: Madhvacharya’s own term for his system, meaning 'the philosophy of reality'.
• **Pancha-Bheda**: The five-fold difference: (1) God vs. Soul, (2) God vs. Matter, (3) Soul vs. Soul, (4) Soul vs. Matter, (5) Matter vs. Matter.
• **Key Metric**: Unlike Shankara’s 'Maya' (illusion), Madhva argued the world is **Satya** (real) and not an illusion.

items.definition: Eight monasteries established by Madhvacharya in Udupi, which rotate the responsibility of worshipping the Krishna idol (Paryaya system).
The relationship where the soul is a reflection (Pratibimba) of the Supreme (Bimba), but never identical to it.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Bhakti as Devotion**: Emphasized 'Bhakti' as the only path to 'Moksha' (liberation).
• **Institutionalization**: Created a robust monastic structure that preserved his teachings for centuries.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Intense intellectual opposition from Advaitins.
• **Solutions**: Prolific writing of 'Bhashyas' (commentaries) on Upanishads, Gita, and Brahma Sutras.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'MAD-V' (Madhva = Dvaita).
• **Decoded Meaning**: M-Madhvacharya, A-Acharya, D-Dvaita, V-Vishnu (Supreme).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses Madhvacharya with Ramanujacharya. Remember: Ramanuja = Vishishtadvaita (Qualified Monism); Madhva = Dvaita (Pure Dualism).
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Theistic Realism' to describe Madhvacharya’s philosophy in answers regarding the evolution of Bhakti.

keyTakeaways: Madhvacharya founded the Dvaita school, asserting the eternal reality of the world and the distinctness of the soul from God.
His institutional legacy is the Udupi Ashta Mathas, which standardized the worship of Lord Krishna.
He rejected the concept of 'Maya' (illusion) central to Advaita Vedanta.
